THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed challenging the Judgment and Award dated 13.04.2012 in MVC No.928/2010 on the file of the Fast Track Court at Udupi, by which, the claim petition is dismissed.

2. Brief facts:
On 26.06.2010 at about about 1.30 p.m, when the petitioner was driving his Maruthi Eeco Car bearing Registration NC: 2023:KHC:20631 No.KA-20-B-7269 from Bajpe Airport to Udupi via Kinnigoli and when he was near Mulki, a Tempo bearing No.KA-20-B-4746 coming from Udupi towards Mangalore in opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner, dashed the petitioner's car and caused heavy damage to petitioner's car.
The damaged vehicle of the claimant was towed and as estimate for repair was issued for a sum of Rs.2,56,806-38 by
Bharath Auto Cars (P) Ltd.

It was Udayananda Prabhu vs Rajesh on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197840241/
2 pleaded that the petitioner was entitled to recover the same from respondents.

sentences.text: R e s p o n d e n t N o . 2 i s t h e r e g i s t e r e d o w n e r o f t h e T e m p o b e a r i n g Reg.No.KA-20-B-4746.
Therefore, the petitioner claimed a total compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- towards damage to the vehicle with interest at 10% p.a., from the date of petition till payment.
Respondent No.3-New India Assurance Co.Ltd., and Respondent No.4-National Insurance Co.Ltd., filed written statement.

Respondent No.3-Insurer of the tempo contended that the accident occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving of Tempo bearing No.KA-20-B-4746 and therefore, the insurer is liable to pay the compensation.

Further, it is contended that the drivers of both the vehicles involved in the accident were not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of alleged accident.
NC: 2023:KHC:20631

It is contended by Respondent No.4 that the driver of the car bearing No.KA-20-B-7269 was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle and the car was not insured with Respondent No.4.
It is further contended that there was contributory negligence on the part of the Respondent No.1, driver of the tempo bearing No.KA-20-B- 4746 as he was rash and negligent in driving the vehicle.
Hence, it is contended that the claim against Respondent No.4 was liable to be dismissed.

The Tribunal framed issues and on examination of the witnesses, held that the petition filed by the claimant was liable to be dismissed as the garage which had issued the estimate was not authorized garage for Maruthi Company and the spare parts are also not genuine.
Hence, the Tribunal dismissed the claim petition filed by the claimant.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
4.
In the present case, the accident is between Maruthi Eeco Car bearing No.KA-20-B-7269 and goods Tempo No. KA-20-B-4746.

The claim petition is filed by the claimant who NC:
2023:KHC:20631 is the owner of the Car, claiming damages of the Maruthi Car, which is extensively damaged.
The claim petition is dismissed on the ground that the car was not got repaired by authorized garage.
Respondent No.3 is the owner of the goods tempo.
The Tribunal has answered Issue No.3 whether the Respondent No.4 (National Insurance Company Limited) proves that it is not a necessary party to this petition, in the negative.
The Tribunal while answering Issue No.3 held that the accident was caused entirely due to the rash and negligent driving of the goods tempo.
Therefore, Respondent No.4-insurer of the Car is not a necessary party.
The Tribunal held that the claim is made against the Respondent Nos.1 to 3.
Respondent No.2 is the owner of goods tempo and Respondent No.3 is the insurer of the tempo.
Since the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the goods tempo, the claim made by the appellant-claimant seeking damages against the Respondents 2 and 3 is maintainable.
5. Ex.P23 is the Estimate given by Abharana Motors for a sum of Rs.2,56,731/-.
Ex.P16 to Ex.P20

are the receipts/tax invoices issued by Sir.Durga Parameshwari Motor Works for a NC:
Udayananda Prabhu vs Rajesh on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197840241/
3 2023:KHC:20631 sum of Rs.2,00,593/- towards repair charges of Maruthi Eco Car.

sentences.text: As far as the estimate given as per Ex.P23 by the authorized showroom of the Maruthi Eeco Car, the car was got repaired as per Ex.P15 to Ex.P21-tax invoices.

PW.2 is the owner of the garage who has deposed that the claimant has got repaired his car in the garage and accordingly, from the evidence of PW.2, it is proved that the appellant/claimant got repaired the car and accordingly, tax invoices as per Ex.P16 to Ex.P20 have been issued.

Therefore, whether the accident is proved by rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tempo and the claimant's car was extensively damaged and for getting repaired the car, estimate was given by PW.3 as per Ex.P23 and it was repaired in the garage of PW.2 and the repair cost is incurred as Rs.2,00,593/- are all proved.
Therefore, Respondents 2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the damages to the claimant.
Since there is a valid insurance policy between Respondents 2 and 3, Respondent No.3-New India Assurance Company Limited is liable to pay damages to the claimant.
Hence, the appeal is liable to be allowed.
The interest on the compensation shall carry at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.

In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The Appeal is allowed.
ii) The appeal against Respondent No.4 is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, it is dismissed.
iii) The Judgment and Award dated 13.04.2012 in MVC No.928/2010 on the file of the Fast Track Court at Udupi, is set aside.

iv) Respondent No.3- New India Assurance Company Limited shall be liable to pay the damages to the claimant at Rs.2,00,593/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realization.
v) No order as to costs.
vi) Draw award accordingly.
